subject.title: [Security] Plaintext credential leakage in diagnostic crash dumps

question: Should this be handled as a confirmed diagnostic-export security defect now, or first require a minimal current-main artifact proving that an escaped credential reaches the generated package?
rationale: Source inspection supports a plausible escaped-JSON redaction gap, but the complete export caller and observable leak have not yet been demonstrated; security owners should decide the disclosure and proof threshold before implementation proceeds.

options.title: Validate Privately, Then Fix
options.body: Reproduce the nested-string leak against the current diagnostic export in a restricted security workflow, then patch the canonical export/redaction boundary and add regression coverage.

options.title: Request Minimal Reproduction
options.body: Ask the reporter for a synthetic credential input, exact export command, affected package member, and redacted verification output before classifying the report as confirmed.

options.title: Prove Existing Sanitization Sufficient
options.body: Close only if an owner traces the full export pipeline and demonstrates that structural sanitization already removes the reported nested credential form.

recommendation.title: Validate Privately, Then Fix
recommendation.body: Reproduce the nested-string leak against the current diagnostic export in a restricted security workflow, then patch the canonical export/redaction boundary and add regression coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history most directly connects this contributor to the current gateway diagnostics export surface.
